A million dollars was meant for a 'Clinton project.' The record can't prove it moved.

Our source audit of the Clinton Foundation, CGI and Epstein tracks five evidence lines: a prospective $1M 2004 Publicis transfer (no matched debit, credit, invoice, or payer), a reported $25K 2006 grant, TerraMar's 2013 CGI participation, and testimony on CGI's origins. Key payment claims remain unverified — and no wrongdoing by anyone named is established by these sources.

Six years before the warrants were quashed, U.S. officials saw the legal playbook coming.

A June 18, 2020 DOJ correspondence records UK officials anticipating Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor's lawyers challenging a mutual legal assistance request by judicial review — a separate proceeding from the 2026 search warrants. Then in July 2026, the High Court quashed those warrants over the wrong statutory basis.

The parallel is real. The two cases are not the same.

New Mexico v. Indyke & Kahn — Epstein executors sued, October 21, 2026.

Attorney General Raúl Torrez filed the first law-enforcement action ever brought against Darren Indyke and Richard Kahn, alleging Epstein's lawyer and accountant "facilitated, financed, and concealed" the trafficking operation, including at Zorro Ranch. Their position for years: no knowledge. The archive's record: Indyke signed FAA filings as Vice President of Shmitka Air, the company that owned Epstein's aircraft (EFTA00016622) — and in May 2017 Kahn was coordinating island flights and answering clearance questions himself (EFTA02213201). Neither name appears in the flight logs. They weren't passengers. They were the office.

The will leaves Indyke $50M and Kahn $25M. New Mexico wants the court to stop it. The men call the suit baseless. Allegations are not findings — the documents are the documents.
